title: Step 4F Preview: Geometry Construction Laboratory Pilots
subject: Mathematics
description: Preview-only validation fixture exercising all four geometry-constructor modes (compass-straightedge, transformations, coordinate-geometry, circle-theorems) plus existing process-stepper reuse for 3D solid nets.

slides.title: 1. Perpendicular Bisector (Arc Provenance)
slides.narration: Construct the perpendicular bisector of segment AB using two equal-radius compass arcs centred at A and B with radius greater than half of AB.

interactive.title: Construct the Perpendicular Bisector of AB
interactive.instructions: Draw two equal-radius compass arcs (radius > 4, e.g. 5) centred at A(-4, 0) and B(4, 0), mark their intersections, and connect them with a straightedge segment.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Perpendicular bisector compass and straightedge construction
interactive.fallbackText: Draw equal arcs of radius 5 from A(-4,0) and B(4,0). Connect their two intersections (0,3) and (0,-3) to form the perpendicular bisector x = 0.
hints: AB has length 8, so choose a compass radius strictly greater than 4 (for example, radius = 5).
Draw arcs of radius 5 centred at A and at B, click Mark Intersections, then connect the two intersection points.
interactive.successExplanation: Every point on this line is equidistant from A and B, and it meets AB at 90° through the midpoint (0, 0).

slides.title: 2. Angle Bisector (Compass Provenance)
slides.narration: Bisect the 90° angle ∠ABC into two equal 45° angles using genuine compass arcs.

interactive.title: Bisect Right Angle ∠ABC
interactive.instructions: Draw an arc centred at vertex B(0, 0), mark its intersections on rays BA and BC, draw two equal arcs from those intersections, mark their meeting point, and connect it to B.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Angle bisector compass and straightedge construction
interactive.fallbackText: Draw an arc from B(0,0) cutting BA and BC at equal distances, then draw two equal arcs from those points to meet along y = x, dividing 90° into two 45° angles.
hints: Start with a compass arc centred at B (e.g. radius 3) and click Mark Intersections.
Draw two equal arcs (e.g. radius 3) from those two ray intersections, mark their intersection, and connect B to it.
interactive.successExplanation: Every point on the bisector is equidistant from rays BA and BC, splitting 90° into two 45° angles.

slides.title: 3. SSS Triangle Construction (Both Orientations)
slides.narration: Construct a 3–4–5 triangle on baseline AB of length 5 using compass arcs of radii 4 and 3.

visual.caption: SSS triangle construction accepting both mirrored orientations.
visual.altText: SSS triangle construction accepting both mirrored orientations.

interactive.title: Construct SSS Triangle with Sides 5, 4, and 3
interactive.instructions: Baseline AB has length 5. Draw an arc of radius 4 from A and an arc of radius 3 from B, mark their intersection C (above or below AB), and connect AC and BC.
interactive.fallbackText: Draw arcs of radius 4 from A(0,0) and radius 3 from B(5,0). Their intersections at (3.2, 2.4) and (3.2, -2.4) both form valid congruent 3-4-5 triangles.
hints: Draw compass arc radius 4 at A, and radius 3 at B.
Click Mark Intersections, then connect either intersection point to both A and B.
interactive.successExplanation: Both mirrored solutions above and below AB are congruent 3–4–5 right-angled triangles.

slides.title: 4. SAS & ASA Triangle Constructions (Multi-Activity Slide)
slides.narration: Construct triangles defined by Side-Angle-Side (SAS) and Angle-Side-Angle (ASA) invariants.

interactive.title: Construct SAS Triangle (AB = 6, AC = 4, ∠BAC = 90°)
interactive.instructions: Place vertex C at distance 4 from A(0, 0) with included angle ∠BAC = 90° (above or below AB).
interactive.fallbackText: Place vertex C at (0, 4) or (0, -4) so that AC = 4 and ∠BAC = 90°.
interactive.successExplanation: Vertex C satisfies |AC| = 4 and included angle ∠BAC = 90°.

interactive.title: Construct ASA Triangle (AB = 6, ∠A = 45°, ∠B = 45°)
interactive.instructions: Place vertex C where the 45° ray from A(0, 0) meets the 45° ray from B(6, 0).
interactive.fallbackText: The 45° rays from A(0,0) and B(6,0) meet at (3, 3) or (3, -3), forming an isosceles right triangle.
interactive.successExplanation: Since ∠A = ∠B = 45°, ∠C = 90° and C lies at (3, 3) or (3, -3).

slides.title: 5. Translation & Reflection Across y = −x (Multi-Activity Slide)
slides.narration: Explore two independent rigid transformations on the same slide: a vector translation and a reflection across the diagonal line y = −x.

interactive.title: Translate Triangle ABC by Vector (3, −2)
interactive.instructions: Move vertices A', B', C' to the image of triangle A(1,3), B(4,3), C(1,5) under translation vector (3, −2).
interactive.successExplanation: Translation preserves size, shape, and orientation.

interactive.title: Reflect Triangle ABC Across y = −x
interactive.instructions: Reflect A(1,2), B(4,2), C(1,4) across the line y = −x. Remember (x, y) maps to (−y, −x).
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Polygon reflection across y equals minus x
interactive.fallbackText: Reflecting across y = -x maps (x, y) to (-y, -x): A'(-2,-1), B'(-2,-4), C'(-4,-1).
interactive.successExplanation: Reflection across y = −x swaps and negates both coordinates.

slides.title: 6. Rotation About a Non-Origin Centre
slides.narration: Rotate triangle ABC by 90° anticlockwise about the non-origin centre (2, 1).

interactive.title: Rotate 90° Anticlockwise About (2, 1)
interactive.instructions: Plot the image of A(4,1), B(6,1), C(4,3) after a 90° anticlockwise rotation about centre (2, 1).
interactive.fallbackText: Subtract (2,1), rotate (dx, dy) -> (-dy, dx), and add (2,1): A'(2,3), B'(2,5), C'(0,3).
interactive.successExplanation: Each vertex shifts by vector (−dy, dx) relative to the centre of rotation (2, 1).

slides.title: 7. Fractional & Negative Enlargement (Multi-Activity Slide)
slides.narration: Investigate enlargements with a fractional scale factor (k = 0.5 on a 0.5-step grid) and a negative scale factor (k = −2, inverting orientation through the centre).

interactive.title: Enlarge by Scale Factor k = 0.5 About (0, 0)
interactive.instructions: Plot the half-scale image of A(1,2), B(5,2), C(1,6) about centre (0, 0). Grid step is 0.5.
interactive.fallbackText: Multiply each coordinate by 0.5: A'(0.5, 1), B'(2.5, 1), C'(0.5, 3).
interactive.successExplanation: Scale factor 0.5 halves every side length and quarters the area.

interactive.title: Enlarge by Negative Scale Factor k = −2 About (0, 0)
interactive.instructions: Plot the inverted image of A(1,1), B(3,1), C(1,2) under enlargement scale factor k = −2 about (0, 0).
interactive.fallbackText: Multiply each coordinate by -2: A'(-2,-2), B'(-6,-2), C'(-2,-4).
interactive.successExplanation: A negative scale factor doubles lengths and projects the image through the centre of enlargement.

slides.title: 8. Horizontal & Vertical Perpendicular Lines
slides.narration: Construct a vertical line perpendicular to a horizontal line without slope-intercept division-by-zero errors.

interactive.title: Vertical Line Perpendicular to y = 2 Through (1, −3)
interactive.instructions: Plot two points P1 and P2 defining the line through T(1, −3) that is perpendicular to the horizontal line y = 2.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Horizontal and vertical perpendicular line workbench
interactive.fallbackText: A line perpendicular to horizontal y = 2 through (1, -3) is the vertical line x = 1 (e.g. P1(1,-3) and P2(1,4)) with undefined gradient.
interactive.successExplanation: The general line form ax + by + c = 0 handles vertical lines (x = 1, gradient undefined) seamlessly.

slides.title: 9. Midpoint & Coordinate Plotting
slides.narration: Find and plot the exact midpoint of segment AB on the Cartesian plane.

interactive.title: Plot the Midpoint of A(−3, 2) and B(5, −4)
interactive.instructions: Click on the grid or enter coordinates for the exact midpoint M of segment AB.
interactive.successExplanation: M(1, −1) averages the x-coordinates and y-coordinates of A and B.

slides.title: 10. Circle Theorem: Angle at Centre & Circumference
slides.narration: Drag point P along the major arc and verify that the angle at the centre is always twice the angle at the circumference.

visual.caption: Angle at centre equals twice angle at circumference.
visual.altText: Angle at centre equals twice angle at circumference.

interactive.title: Angle at Centre vs Angle at Circumference
interactive.instructions: Move P along the major arc (between 330° and 210° via 90°). Observe ∠AOB = 120° and deduce ∠APB.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Angle at centre circle theorem explorer
interactive.fallbackText: When minor arc AB subtends 120° at centre O, any point P on the major arc gives ∠APB = 60°.

circleTheorem.targetPrompt: With ∠AOB = 120° on the minor arc, what is the invariant angle ∠APB on the major arc?

slides.title: 11. Cyclic Quadrilateral & Tangent–Radius (Multi-Activity Slide)
slides.narration: Verify opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°, and confirm a tangent meets the radius at 90°.

interactive.title: Opposite Angles of a Cyclic Quadrilateral
interactive.instructions: Keep P on the arc opposite C(90°). With chord A(210°)–B(330°), opposite angle ∠ACB = 60°; deduce ∠APB.
interactive.fallbackText: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°, so ∠APB = 180° - 60° = 120°.

circleTheorem.targetPrompt: Since opposite angle ∠ACB = 60°, what must ∠APB equal?

interactive.successExplanation: ∠APB + ∠ACB = 120° + 60° = 180° for every non-crossing position of P.

interactive.title: Tangent Meets Radius at 90°
interactive.instructions: Inspect radius OA and the tangent at A and verify the angle between them.
interactive.fallbackText: A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular (90°) to the radius at the point of contact.

circleTheorem.targetPrompt: What angle does the tangent line always make with radius OA?

interactive.successExplanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at every point on the circumference.

slides.title: 12. Locus Construction (Fixed Distance from a Point)
slides.narration: Construct the exact locus of all points at fixed distance 4 units from point O(0, 0).

interactive.title: Locus of Points at Distance 4 from O(0, 0)
interactive.instructions: Use the compass tool to draw the complete circle centred at O(0, 0) with radius 4.
interactive.fallbackText: The locus of all points at distance 4 from O(0,0) is the circle centred at O with radius 4.
interactive.successExplanation: The analytical circle x² + y² = 16 represents every point exactly 4 units from O.

slides.title: 13. Solid Geometry Nets (Reusing Existing Process Stepper)
slides.narration: Explore how a 2D net folds into a 3D square-based pyramid using the existing process-stepper engine — zero duplicate engine code required.

visual.caption: 3D solid net folding sequence via process-stepper.
visual.altText: 3D solid net folding sequence via process-stepper.

interactive.title: Folding a Square-Based Pyramid Net
interactive.instructions: Step through how the flat 2D net folds along its four base edges to form a 3D square-based pyramid.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Step-by-step folding of a square-based pyramid net
interactive.fallbackText: A square-based pyramid net has 1 square base and 4 congruent isosceles triangles that fold up to meet at a single apex (5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices).

stages.title: Flat 2D Net
stages.summary: Lay out 1 square base surrounded by 4 congruent isosceles triangles. Total faces = 1 square + 4 triangles = 5 faces.

stages.title: Fold Along Base Edges
stages.summary: Lift all four triangular faces upward along the four edges of the square base; each base edge is shared by the square and one triangle.

stages.title: Meet at the Apex
stages.summary: The four triangle tips meet at a single top vertex (apex), sealing 4 slant edges. Euler's formula holds: V − E + F = 5 − 8 + 5 = 2.
